title: Design System: Le Nguyen Thanh Ha — AI Product Engineer

display.purpose: Four or five headline moments. Uppercase, condensed, authored line breaks inside clipping wrappers.

label.purpose: Monospace metadata, eyebrows, chips, instrument readout. Uppercase in Latin locales only.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system. Hover and focus on a work card, always alongside the inset highlight.

shadows.name: lift-light
shadows.purpose: Same role in the light theme, where 60% black is too heavy on cream.

shadows.name: inset-highlight
shadows.purpose: The lit top edge that gives a surface material. Light theme uses rgba(255,255,255,.85).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The signature curve. Every state change and entrance. Do not introduce a second ease-out.

motion.name: ease-acquire
motion.purpose: One-shot acquisition: the bracket closing on a target.

motion.name: duration-reduced
motion.purpose: Everything that survives prefers-reduced-motion: colour, border, outline, opacity, visibility.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: One per view. Signal red fill, ground ink, full pill.

components.name: Work Card
components.description: Schematic, claim, tags, verifiable figure, route to check it.

components.name: Reel Step
components.description: Numbered jump target under the pinned card rail. Accessible name comes from its card's heading.

components.name: Acquisition Bracket
components.description: The system's single motif. Four L-corners at a fixed 17px, drawn around any target regardless of its size.

narrative.overview:
The page is built as a piece of detection equipment rather than as a portfolio. Its subject builds computer-vision systems that watch a room and report what they saw, and the interface performs that same job on itself: a reticle tracks the cursor, a canvas acquires ambient targets behind the headline, a fixed instrument locks onto whichever section you have reached, and brackets close around the heading you jump to. The bracket is the single motif and it appears at every scale.

The ground is a cold near-black lit by one warm aubergine bloom, with warm cream text that is never pure white and a single signal red used sparingly enough that it always means look here. A 22px dot lattice and a fine grain sit under everything, so the background reads as a sensor surface rather than as a void.

The confirmed anti-reference is the AI-SaaS marketing page: gradient text, glass panels, pastel abstractions, icon-heading-paragraph card grids, and stock illustration of AI. Every claim is attached to a number and a route to verify it.
keyCharacteristics: One motif — the acquisition bracket — carried through eight surfaces
Cold ground, warm ink, one signal colour
Instrumentation over decoration: labels are monospace and measured, prose is serif
Evidence typography: every figure tabular, every claim ending in a checkable number
Four locales as a first-class constraint, not a retrofit

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Red marks exactly one thing per view: the action, the current position, or the figure being claimed. When two elements both want it, one of them is wrong about its importance.

rules.name: The Warm Ink Rule
rules.body: No pure white and no pure black as ink. The only pure values in the system are the image outline and the inset highlight, where a tinted neutral would read as dirt on a photograph.

rules.name: The Two Unit Rule
rules.body: Text sizes are rem so the page answers the reader's own browser font size. Display type stays px + vw because those lines are authored to break on specific words and live inside overflow:hidden.

rules.name: The Short Caps Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is for labels, never for sentences. Keys are uppercase; their values are not. Removed entirely under :lang(ja) and :lang(zh).

rules.name: The Lit Edge Rule
rules.body: A surface reads as material because of an inset top highlight, not a drop shadow. Any rule setting box-shadow on a card must re-state the inset.

dos: Do attach every claim to a number and a route to check it.
Do re-state the inset highlight in any rule that sets box-shadow on a card.
Do use rem for anything a reader reads and px + vw for authored display lines.
Do gate pointer-driven depth behind (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine).
Do keep uppercase to labels, and remove it entirely under :lang(ja) and :lang(zh).
Do name any new curve against --ease-out rather than introducing a second ease-out.
donts: Don't put body copy on the signal red, or use red for two meanings on one screen.
Don't use pure white or pure black as ink.
Don't add a tinted border to a photograph; use outline with --img-outline.
Don't add a string without adding it to all three dictionaries and running design/i18n/sync.py.
Don't animate a layout property, and don't let decorative animation survive prefers-reduced-motion — but do keep opacity and visibility transitions.
Don't introduce a third-party origin on the critical path.
